messages:
sam_sales: Kicking off POC networking checklist for the Acme deal. They asked for PrivateLink but Infosec also wants a short allowlist for any fallbacks. Can we confirm exact requirements?
aya_solutions: Quick summary: PrivateLink = interface endpoints in customer VPC, no outbound internet required for API traffic. Hosted API = outbound TLS 443 to our public endpoints (so need egress allowlist or proxy exceptions).
devin_neteng: To add — PrivateLink workflow: we give a service name (com.amazonaws.vpce-svc-...), customer creates interface endpoints in the required subnets/AZs, then they share the vpce IDs for us to accept. Security groups on the endpoint must allow inbound TCP 443 from their app subnets.
kevin_eng: Note on static IPs: for Hosted API we can provide a small set of egress NAT IPs per region for firewall allowlisting. For PrivateLink you do NOT need those IPs. Hosted egress example (NOT real prod): 54.203.10.12/32, 34.201.2.3/32 — customer should only allow TCP/443 to those.
sam_sales: Acme's security questionnaire specifically asks: "Can you provide IPs and FQDNs to allow? Do you support mTLS? What about proxy and TLS interception?"
aya_solutions: Answers to Qs: 
- IPs/FQDNs: For Hosted -> we provide region egress IPs and recommend also allowing api.redwood.ai. For PrivateLink -> provide endpoint service name.
- mTLS: supported for Dedicated and Private deployments. Hosted API doesn't support customer mTLS by default.
- TLS inspection / corporate proxy: If they terminate TLS in transit (MITM), that may break integrity checks for hosted API. Recommend PrivateLink or Dedicated in that case.
devin_neteng: POC checklist for customer (short):
1) Tell us which model/route they want (Hosted vs PrivateLink vs Dedicated).
2) If PrivateLink: create interface endpoints in 2 AZs, open SGs for TCP/443 from app subnets, give us vpce-ids.
3) If Hosted: add outbound firewall rule to allow TCP/443 to our egress IPs or allowlist api.redwood.ai.
4) If corporate HTTP proxy: share proxy host/port and whether it does TLS inspection.
5) If they need mTLS: plan for Dedicated or Private deployment.

devin_neteng: Sample SG rules they can paste into their ticket:```
# Interface endpoint SG (Attach to vpce ENIs)
Inbound: HTTPS TCP 443 
  Source: 10.10.0.0/20   # app subnet or app SG
Outbound: All traffic 0.0.0.0/0
```

kevin_eng: And sample firewall rules for Hosted API allowlist:```
# Perimeter FW outbound rules
Destination: 54.203.10.12/32, 34.201.2.3/32   # our region egress IPs (example)
Ports: TCP 443
Purpose: allow API calls to api.redwood.ai
```

sam_sales: They asked about DNS vs IP allowlist — they prefer DNS. Is that OK?
aya_solutions: DNS allowlist is fine but many corporate firewalls prefer IPs. We can give both: api.redwood.ai + region egress IPs. Warn them IPs can change if they rely solely on ephemeral infra; PrivateLink avoids that problem.
devin_neteng: Testing tips after they create endpoint:
- curl test to the customer-side DNS: `curl -v https://vpce-<id>.execute-api.<region>.amazonaws.com/health` (or whatever endpoint we provide)
- Confirm SG allows 443 from app subnet
- Share vpce-id with us so we accept the endpoint on our side

sam_sales: Action items: I'll request the PrivateLink service name and final egress IP list from infra (need by EOD). @devin_neteng can you draft the short step-by-step we can attach to the security questionnaire?
devin_neteng: Yup, I'll drop a one-pager with SG rules + firewall snippets and a failover note that Hosted->PrivateLink migration requires reconfiguring endpoint and DNS.
kevin_eng: deploy-bot: NOTE: generated current placeholder service name for POC: com.amazonaws.vpce-svc-0ef123abcd (will replace with real) :gear:
deploy-bot: service-name com.amazonaws.vpce-svc-0ef123abcd"
